MKI · Jellyfin plugin

Screen Fit

Plays the Full HD version of a movie on screens that cannot show 4K, and makes transcodes only as large as the screen. Bitrate limits and transcode throttling stay exactly as you set them in Jellyfin.

What the plugin does

For every user, on the devices whose screen is known.

For movies with a 4K and a Full HD version, for example merged by MKI Merge Versions. Only when both are the same cut and the Full HD one has the chosen audio and subtitle language; otherwise 4K stays. Works for direct play too: the player simply gets the Full HD file.
For videos Jellyfin transcodes anyway, for example for a codec or HDR the device cannot play, burned-in subtitles or a bitrate limit. Example: a movie that only exists in 4K, started on a Full HD laptop, is transcoded to 1920×1080 instead of 4K. It looks the same there, and the server encodes a quarter of the pixels. Never smaller than 1280×720. This switch never touches direct playing, remuxing or direct streaming.

How it decides

Each time a video starts, before Jellyfin answers the player.

monitor1 · Screen Measured or set Browsers and apps built on the web client measure their screen. For TV apps you set it per device. Stops here when the screen is unknown or doubtful (TV browsers, privacy settings). Only a movie last watched in Full HD is put back to 4K.
swap_horiz2 · Version Full HD file on a Full HD screen Screens up to 1200 pixels on the shorter side: 1080p monitors, most laptops, phones. 4K stays for another cut, a missing audio or subtitle language, a version picked by hand, or when the player would need more work for the Full HD file (a transcode it would not need for 4K).
photo_size_select_large3 · Transcode Only as large as the screen At most the screen's size, never below 1280×720. Only when Jellyfin transcodes the video anyway. Direct playing, remuxing and direct streaming stay as they are.
  • speedNever changes bitrate limits, transcode throttling, codecs or audio. The resume position carries over between versions.
  • restoreA movie started in Full HD on a laptop resumes in 4K on the TV, and on every screen not known to be Full HD, unless that player needs more work for the 4K file. A version someone picks by hand stays theirs.
  • groupA device setting only changes what plays on that device, for whoever uses it. It does not grant or block anything.
